The Secy. Ministry Of Road Transport And Highways
Counsel for Applicant :- Himanshu Raghave
Hon'ble Mrs. Sangeeta Chandra,J.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.
This is an application for review of our order dated 15.04.2024.

The main ground taken by the
counsel for the applicants praying for review of the order is that in para 10 of the order a mention
has been made of the arguments raised by the counsel for the Nhai which is misleading in nature.
Para 10 states that main relief claimed by the petitioners is for quashing of the award notified on 03.05.2023 and statutory remedy under Section 3(G)(5) of the NHAI Act is available.
The counsel for the applicants says that no relief was claimed for quashing of the award dated 03.05.2023 by the petitioners.
Balram Singh And Others vs Union Of India Thru.

1 2. We have gone through the relief clause of the writ petition and we find from the same that the petitioners had prayed for quashing of notification issued under Section 3(D)(2) dated 03.05.2023 filed as annexure No. 1 to the writ petition.

3. We have gone through the annexure no. 1 i.e. notification issued under Section 3(D)(2) which is in the nature of a final notification for acquisition of the plot numbers mentioned therein of various villages in the district of Lucknow and Unnao.

The petitioners' village Banthra Sikanderpur is at internal page 7 of the said notification and it refers to Gata Nos. 449, 463, 538 as land belonging to the Government recorded as abadi and non-agricultural.

The counsel for the petitioners says that against acquisition notification under Section 3(D)(2) of the Act no remedy is provided under Section 3(G)(5) and a misleading argument was made by the counsel appearing for NHAI.
4. We have considered the provisions of the Act and we find that any notification issued under Section 3(D)(2) becomes final under Section 3(D)(4) of the Act.

However, we find from the acquisition notification itself, annexure 1 to the petition, that the land mentioned as plot nos. 449,
463 and 538 are Government land of village abadi and therefore, no acquisition of such government land by the government is necessary.
The petitioners have raised their houses over such land for which compensation was given to them ex gratia as per the government order applicable in this regard.
In the writ petition itself a mention has been made of the amount that was deposited for compensation of the superstructure raised by the petitioners on a government land.

In the order passed by us on 15.04.2024, arguments raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners regarding the petitioners not wanting compensation at all has been noted in para 6 of our order wherein it has been stated that the petitioners do not want any ex gratia payment that was determined for them.
They are entitled for compensation as per the new Act of 2013 being owner of the land on which their constructions is situated.

They had been given compensation only for constructions raised by them on such land and that the petitioners' land was being acquired deviating from the original Detailed Project Report which did not provide for alignment as shown at the curve at Banthra village.

5. We are of the considered opinion that after notices were issued to the petitioners regarding removal of their encroachment on government land/abadi land which has been mentioned as such in the notification dated 03.05.2024 and ex gratia payment was offered to them for the constructions they had raised over it, they could not have challenged the notification under Section 3(D)(2) by which the government determined to take that land that belonged to the government, but was in occupation of the petitioners.
Therefore, the first relief prayed for in the relief clause could not have been finally given to the petitioners.

6. With regard to the other arguments raised by the learned counsel for the review applicants that the applicants have not made any prayer for compensation, it is evident from a perusal of para 6 itself of the order dated 15.04.2024 that such an argument was not made by the counsel for the petitioners at the time of hearing of the writ petition.
Para 6 of the order dated 15.04.2024 has been carefully perused by us.
The review applicants seek re-hearing of the matter on merit which cannot be done in the review petition.
Balram Singh And Others vs Union Of India Thru.

2 7.
The scope of review of an order is very limited and no error apparent on the face of record could be shown by the counsel for the applicants to us to exercise the limited jurisdiction.
8. In view of the above discussion, the review application stands rejected.
